questions.stem: What is crash consistency in file systems?

options.text: The ability to maintain a consistent state after a crash during write operations.
The ability to recover deleted files after a crash.
The ability to prevent crashes during write operations.
The ability to improve write performance during normal operations.

questions.explanation: Crash consistency ensures that a file system remains in a consistent state even if a crash occurs during write operations. It does not prevent crashes or recover deleted files.

distractorRationale.b: This describes data recovery, not crash consistency.
distractorRationale.c: Crash consistency does not prevent crashes; it deals with their aftermath.
distractorRationale.d: Improving write performance is not directly related to crash consistency.

questions.stem: How does journalling help in maintaining file system consistency?

options.text: By preventing crashes during write operations.
By logging changes before applying them to the file system.
By increasing the speed of write operations.
By automatically recovering deleted files.

questions.explanation: Journalling maintains file system consistency by recording changes in a log before they are applied. This allows the system to replay or roll back changes after a crash.

distractorRationale.a: Journalling does not prevent crashes; it helps recover from them.
distractorRationale.c: Journalling may slow down write operations due to the additional logging step.
distractorRationale.d: Journalling is not designed for recovering deleted files.

questions.stem: A file system writes 100 MB of data with journalling enabled. If the journalling overhead is 10%, how much total data is written to the disk? Provide your answer in MB.
questions.explanation: The journalling overhead means an additional 10% of the data size is written to the journal. Thus, 100 MB + 10% of 100 MB = 110 MB is written to the disk.

questions.stem: What is the primary trade-off when using write caching in file systems?

options.text: Increased performance vs. reduced durability.
Increased durability vs. reduced performance.
Increased security vs. reduced usability.
Increased usability vs. reduced security.

questions.explanation: Write caching improves performance by delaying writes to disk, but it risks data loss if a crash occurs before the cache is flushed, reducing durability.

distractorRationale.b: Write caching typically increases performance at the cost of durability.
distractorRationale.c: This trade-off is not related to write caching.
distractorRationale.d: This trade-off is not related to write caching.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of a journal in a file system?

options.text: A backup of all files in the system.
A log of changes to be applied to the file system.
A cache of frequently accessed files.
A record of user access permissions.

questions.explanation: The journal logs changes to ensure they can be completed or rolled back after a crash, maintaining file system consistency.

distractorRationale.a: A journal is not a backup; it logs changes for consistency.
distractorRationale.c: A journal is not a cache; it logs changes.
distractorRationale.d: A journal does not record access permissions.

questions.stem: If a file system with write caching enabled writes 200 MB of data and only 150 MB is committed to disk before a crash, how much data is potentially lost? Provide your answer in MB.
questions.explanation: With write caching, 200 MB was intended to be written, but only 150 MB was committed to disk. Thus, 200 MB - 150 MB = 50 MB of data is potentially lost.

questions.stem: Why might a file system choose not to use journalling?

options.text: To reduce write overhead and improve performance.
To increase the complexity of the file system.
To ensure all data is immediately written to disk.
To improve security by avoiding logs.

questions.explanation: Journalling introduces write overhead due to logging, which can impact performance. Some systems may avoid it to improve write speed.

distractorRationale.b: Avoiding journalling does not increase complexity.
distractorRationale.c: Journalling does not prevent immediate writes; it logs changes.
distractorRationale.d: Journalling is not primarily a security feature.
